what_its_for: This medicine is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). It contains two medicines in one capsule. Amlodipine is a calcium channel blocker that relaxes and widens your blood vessels. Benazepril is an ACE inhibitor that helps your heart pump blood more easily. Together, they help lower your blood pressure and reduce your risk of heart attack and stroke.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth once a day, with or without food. Swallow the capsule whole — do not crush, chew, or open it. Try to take it at the same time every day so you do not forget. Even if you feel fine, keep taking this medicine. High blood pressure often has no symptoms, but it can cause serious harm if left untreated.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you. Common starting doses range from amlodipine 2.5 mg / benazepril 10 mg up to amlodipine 10 mg / benazepril 40 mg per day. Your doctor may adjust your dose over time based on how your blood pressure responds. Always follow your doctor's instructions and never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — as long as it is the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next scheduled dose as usual. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. Taking double doses can cause your blood pressure to drop too low.
storage: Store at room temperature between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of the reach of children and pets. Do not use it after the expiration date printed on the package. Ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of unused medicine.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking potassium supplements or using salt substitutes that contain potassium unless your doctor tells you it is okay, as this medicine can raise potassium levels in your blood. Limit alcohol, because it can further lower your blood pressure and cause dizziness or fainting. Be careful standing up quickly from a sitting or lying position to avoid feeling lightheaded. Avoid NSAIDs (like ibuprofen or naproxen) without asking your doctor, as they can reduce how well this medicine works. Do not use this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant — it can cause serious harm to an unborn baby.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat (this is called angioedema and can be life-threatening); difficulty breathing or swallowing; a sudden drop in blood pressure causing severe dizziness or fainting; chest pain; signs of high potassium such as muscle weakness or irregular heartbeat; signs of kidney problems such as little or no urination; severe skin rash or itching; or if you become pregnant while taking this medicine. Also call your doctor if you develop a persistent dry cough, which is a common side effect of benazepril.
when_it_works: Amlodipine and benazepril start working within a few hours of your first dose. However, it may take 1 to 2 weeks of regular use before you notice the full benefit in lowering your blood pressure. Your doctor will check your blood pressure regularly to make sure the medicine is working. Continue taking it even when you feel well — stopping suddenly can cause your blood pressure to spike.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Do NOT take this medicine if you are pregnant. It can cause serious injury or death to an unborn baby. Tell your doctor immediately if you become pregnant. Breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding, as this medicine may pass into breast milk. Kidney disease: Your doctor may need to adjust your dose or monitor your kidneys more closely. Liver disease: Use with caution; your doctor will monitor you carefully. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to the blood pressure-lowering effects and may be at higher risk for dizziness and falls. Children: This medicine is not typically recommended for children. Always tell your doctor and pharmacist about all other medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take to avoid dangerous interactions.
